items.question:
다음 문장에서 'board'의 뜻으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
Let's play a board game.
items.explanation: 문맥에서 'board game'은 '보드 게임'을 의미하며, 여기서 'board'는 '판'이나 '널빤지'를 뜻합니다.

items.question: Choose the word closest in meaning to careful.
items.explanation: 'careful'은 '조심하는, 주의 깊은'이라는 뜻으로, 'cautious'와 가장 유사한 의미를 가집니다.

items.question:
다음 문장에서 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 알맞은 단어는?
My hobby is to _______ stamps from different countries.
items.explanation: 문맥상 '다른 나라의 우표를 모으는 것'이 취미라는 내용이므로, '모으다'라는 의미의 'collect'가 가장 적절합니다.

items.question:
다음 문장에서 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 고르시오.
"My brother often _____ video games after school."
items.explanation: 주어가 3인칭 단수 (My brother)이고, 'often'이 현재 습관을 나타내므로 현재 시제 동사에 -s를 붙인 'plays'가 적절합니다.

items.question:
다음 문장에서 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 고르시오.
"You _____ wear a helmet when you ride a bicycle."
items.explanation: 자전거를 탈 때 헬멧을 착용하는 것이 좋다는 권유나 충고의 의미이므로 'should'가 가장 적절합니다. 'must'는 의무, 'can'은 능력, 'will'은 미래를 나타냅니다.

items.question:
다음 문장에서 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 고르시오.
"The concert starts _____ 7 p.m. _____ Friday."
items.explanation: 특정 시각 앞에는 'at'을 사용하고, 요일 앞에는 'on'을 사용합니다. 따라서 'at 7 p.m. on Friday'가 올바른 표현입니다.

items.question:
다음 문장에서 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 고르시오.
"She speaks English very _____."
items.explanation: 동사 'speaks'를 수식하는 것은 부사이므로, 형용사 'good'의 부사형인 'well'이 적절합니다. 'better'와 'best'는 비교급과 최상급입니다.

items.question: 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
options: 마이클의 어머니는 아들의 숙제 기한 연장을 요청한다.
마이클은 학교에서 종종 늦게 집에 온다.
items.explanation: 이 글은 마이클의 어머니가 아들이 너무 피곤해서 숙제를 끝내지 못했으니 주말에 숙제를 해서 다음 주 월요일에 제출할 수 있도록 허락해 달라고 선생님께 요청하는 내용이다.
items.passage: Dear Ms. White, My son, Michael, got home from school yesterday around 6 p.m. after the basketball match, with four homework assignments. By 11 p.m., he had completed only three: science, math and English. He worked hard all evening. When he was about to start your homework, I decided to stop him. He looked exhausted, so I made him pack up his books and go to bed. I promised him that I would write to you and explain the situation. Michael is anxious to finish your homework. Would it be possible to allow him to do it over the weekend and hand it in next Monday? We would be very grateful if you could agree to this. Yours sincerely, Dorothy Williams

items.question: 글에 따르면, 필자는 은행 명세서에서 어떤 문제를 발견했는가?
options: 결제 문제로 티켓을 구매할 수 없었다.
items.explanation: 필자는 은행 명세서를 확인했을 때 자신의 신용 카드가 두 번 청구된 것을 발견했다고 명시되어 있다.
items.passage: My wife and I visited your cinema last month. We purchased two tickets which came to a total of $44. At the time of purchase, the attendant at the information desk told us they were having some problems accepting credit card payments. At that time, I was anxious about my credit card payment, but the attendant told me that there was no problem with my payment. However, when I received my bank statement, I discovered that you charged my card twice. I would be grateful if you could resolve this matter quickly.

items.question: 윗글을 바탕으로 화이트 선생님에 대해 추론할 수 있는 것은 무엇인가?
items.explanation: 편지의 내용이 마이클의 숙제에 대한 요청이며, '당신의 숙제(your homework)'라는 표현을 사용한 것으로 보아 화이트 선생님은 마이클의 선생님임을 추론할 수 있다.

items.question: 이 편지의 주된 목적은 무엇인가?

items.question:

items.explanation: 콤마 뒤에 사람을 설명하는 관계대명사이므로 'who'가 적절합니다. 'that'은 계속적 용법(콤마 뒤)에 올 수 없습니다.

items.question:

items.explanation: 'would travel'을 통해 가정법 과거임을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 if절에는 과거 시제 동사 'had'가 와야 합니다.

items.question: 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
options: 선택의 폭이 넓을수록 오히려 불행과 후회를 야기할 수 있다.
비교를 통해 최선의 선택을 하는 것이 중요하다.
사람들은 항상 더 많은 선택권을 가지기를 원한다.
선택의 자유는 언제나 개인의 만족도를 높인다.
items.explanation: 이 글은 선택의 폭이 넓어질수록 사람들이 오히려 결정을 내리지 못하거나, 내린 결정에 대해 후회하며 불행감을 느낄 수 있다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. '선택의 폭정'이라는 개념을 통해 이러한 역설적인 상황을 강조합니다.
items.passage: Shoppers confronted with the choice of thirty different varieties of gourmet chocolates are more likely to walk away without buying any, compared with when they are presented with only half a dozen choices. If employees are given a free trip to Paris, they are happy. If you give them a free trip to Hawaii, they are happy. But if you offer them the choice between the two destinations, they are less happy, no matter what they choose. Why might choice be so (a) disruptive ? The reason is that choice forces us to make comparisons and acknowledge relative (b) disadvantages . People who choose Paris complain that it doesn’t have the ocean and those who choose Hawaii regret that it doesn’t have the museums. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the ‘tyranny of choice’ because rather than providing freedom, it actually (c) constrains our decision-making. He argues that (d) narrower choice increases unhappiness because we worry that we are going to make the wrong decision and so we get stressed about trying to process all the comparisons in an effort to get it right. This both increases our fear of making the wrong choice and raises expectations that we should be able to get the best choice. Having made the choice, we then (e) start to regret, wondering whether it was the right one.

items.question: 필자가 마라톤 전에 사과 버터를 먹었을 때 어떤 일이 일어났는가?
options: 마라톤 도중 여러 번 멈춰야 했다.
items.explanation: 필자는 마라톤 전날 사과 버터를 먹고 다음 날 'the apple butter forced me to make several stops during the marathon'이라고 언급하며, 이로 인해 경주 중 여러 번 멈춰야 했다고 설명합니다.
items.passage: One of the most important things to remember before a race is to eat the right foods. Here is my lesson for you. The night before one of my marathons, I was struck by an uncontrollable need for apple butter. I satisfied the hunger that evening but paid a heavy price the next day; the apple butter forced me to make several stops during the marathon. You can bet that I never ate apple butter again before a race. Instead, I concentrate on foods that are part of my normal diet such as pasta and rice: foods that fuel my muscles. You must certainly have similar foods that you eat every day. These foods are the ones you should concentrate on before a race.

items.question: 윗글의 내용으로 미루어 볼 때, '선택의 폭정(tyranny of choice)'이 시사하는 바는 무엇인가?
options: 선택은 자유를 주기보다는 심리적 부담과 후회를 야기할 수 있다.
사람들은 항상 더 많은 선택권을 원하며, 이는 만족으로 이어진다.
완벽한 선택을 하는 것은 불가능하므로, 선택은 무의미하다.
선택의 어려움은 주로 물질적인 것에 국한된다.
items.explanation: 글에 따르면 '선택의 폭정'은 선택이 자유를 제공하기보다 의사 결정을 제약하고, 비교와 후회를 불러일으키며, 잘못된 선택에 대한 두려움과 최선에 대한 기대를 증가시켜 불행을 초래한다고 설명합니다.
items.passage: Shoppers confronted with the choice of thirty different varieties of gourmet chocolates are more likely to walk away without buying any, compared with when they are presented with only half a dozen choices. If employees are given a free trip to Paris, they are happy. If you give them a free trip to Hawaii, they are happy. But if you offer them the choice between the two destinations, they are less happy, no matter what they choose. Why might choice be so (a) disruptive ? The reason is that choice forces us to make comparisons and acknowledge relative (b) disadvantages . People who choose Paris complain that it doesn’t have the ocean and those who choose Hawaii regret that it doesn’t have the museums. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the ‘tyranny of choice’ because rather than providing freedom, it actually (c) constrains our decision-making. He argues that (d) narrower choice increases unhappiness because we worry that we are going to make the wrong decision and so we get stressed about trying to process all the comparisons in an effort to get it right. This both increases our fear of making the wrong choice and raises expectations that we should be able to get the best choice. Having made the choice, we then (e) start to regret, wondering whether it was the right one.

items.question: 윗글의 필자가 이 글을 쓴 주된 목적은 무엇인가?

items.passage: One of the most important things to remember before a race is to eat the right foods. Here is my lesson for you. You can bet that I never ate apple butter again before a race. Instead, I concentrate on foods that are part of my normal diet such as pasta and rice: foods that fuel my muscles. You must certainly have similar foods that you eat every day. These foods are the ones you should concentrate on before a race.

items.passage: Nathaniel Adams Cole was born in Alabama on March 17, 1919. Cole learned piano from his mother, and both he and his older brother Eddie became professional musicians by their teens. As a teenager Cole organized two musical groups, the Rogues of Rhythm and the Royal Dukes. At 15, he dropped out of school to become a full-time jazz piano player. After he found a job as a pianist at the Century Club in Santa Monica, he formed a trio with Oscar Moore and Wesley Prince in 1939. In 1951, however, the trio officially broke up. After that, Cole emerged as a popular solo vocalist. He released more than forty albums and contributed to the introduction of “race music” to the larger American musical scene.

items.passage:
Although we humans are equipped with reflexive responses for survival, at birth we are (a) helpless . We spend about a year unable to walk, about two more before we can articulate full thoughts, and many more years unable to provide for ourselves. We are totally dependent on those around us for our survival. Now compare this to many other mammals. Dolphins, for instance,are born swimming; giraffes learn to stand within hours; a baby zebra can run within forty-five minutes of birth. Across the animal kingdom, our cousins are strikingly (b) independent soon after they’re born.

  On the face of it, that seems like a great advantage for other species ― but in fact it signifies a limitation. Baby animals develop quickly because their brains are wiring up according to a largely preprogrammed routine. But that (c) preparedness trades off with flexibility. Imagine if some unfortunate rhinoceros found itself on the Arctic tundra, or on top of a mountain in the Himalayas, or in the middle of a metropolis. It would have no capacity to adapt (which is why we don’t find rhinos in those areas). This strategy of arriving with a pre-arranged brain works inside a particular niche in the ecosystem ― but put an animal outside of that niche, and its chances of thriving are (d) low .

  In contrast, humans are able to thrive in many different environments, from the frozen tundra to the high mountains to crowded urban centers. This is possible because the human brain is born remarkably incomplete. Instead of arriving with everything wired up ― let’s call it “hardwired” ― a human brain (e) forbids itself to be shaped by the details of life experience. This leads to long periods of helplessness as the young brain slowly molds to its environment. It’s “livewired.”

* niche: 적합한 장소

As a couple start to form a relationship, they can be seen to develop a set of constructs about their own relationship and, in particular, how it is similar or different to their parents’ relationship. The couple’s initial disclosures involve them forming constructs about how much similarity there is between them and each other’s families. What each of them will remember is selective and (a) coloured by their family’s constructs system. In turn it is likely that as they tell each other their already edited stories, there is a second process of editing whereby what they both hear from each other is again (b) interpreted within their respective family of origin’s construct systems. The two sets of memories ― the person talking about his or her family and the partner’s edited version of this story ― go into the ‘cooking-pot’ of the couple’s new construct system. Subsequently, one partner may (c) randomly recall a part of the other’s story as a tactic in negotiations: for example, Harry may say to Doris that she is being ‘bossy ― just like her mother’. Since this is probably based on what Doris has told Harry, this is likely to be a very powerful tactic. She may protest or attempt to rewrite this version of her story, thereby possibly adding further material that Harry could use in this way. These exchanges of stories need not always be (d) employed in such malevolent ways. These reconstructed memories can become very powerful, to a point where each partner may become confused even about the simple (e) factual details of what actually did happen in their past.

* malevolent: 악의 있는

items.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: To illustrate the diverse meanings of idioms containing the word "hand".
To warn against the misuse of common English idioms related to "hand".
To provide a historical overview of the word "hand" in English expressions.
To encourage readers to learn more English vocabulary and its origins.
items.explanation: 지문은 'hand'를 사용한 여러 영어 표현들을 소개하고 각각의 의미를 자세히 설명하고 있으므로, 이러한 표현들의 다양한 의미를 보여주는 것이 글의 주된 내용입니다.
items.passage:
There are hundreds of expressions of words using "hand" in the English language. Let us examine some of the expressions that use "hand".
We will get a hand in this way. "To get a hand in" is to begin a job, to begin to know something about it. When we learn completely, we will be able to do it hands down. If we do the job well, we may end up with the upper hand. On the other hand, if the situation gets out of hand, it is out of control.
We must consider another way of expressing phrase---- to hand it to someone. For example, I must hand it to you for understanding what we have discussed this far. You can also lend a hand to someone but without really giving up your hand. You lend a hand when you help someone. If someone is kind enough to lend us a hand then we surely do not want to bite the hand that feeds us. We do not want to repay his kindness by treating him badly.
Now, we have a free hand to continue examining other "hand" expressions. It means you are free to act without getting permission from someone else.

items.question: What can be inferred about the narrator's primary motivation for establishing Pontinha as his own country?
options: A deep desire for absolute personal freedom and autonomy.
A goal to avoid paying taxes in Portugal and other obligations.
An ambition to create a profitable tourist attraction for financial gain.
A wish to prove his family and friends wrong about his sanity.
items.explanation: 화자는 '무엇이든 될 수 있고', '국기를 언제든 바꿀 수 있으며', '절대적인 권력을 가진다'고 말하며, 수영 금지 구역에서도 자유롭게 수영할 수 있음을 언급합니다. 이는 그가 개인적인 자유와 자율성을 매우 중요하게 생각했음을 추론하게 합니다.
items.passage:
My father wasn't a king, he was a taxi driver, but I am a prince-Prince Renato II, of the country Pontinha, an island fort on Funchal harbour. It's in Madeira,Portugal, where I grew up. It was discovered in 1419.
In 1903, the king of Portugal sold the land to a wealthy British family, the Blandys, who make Madeira wine. Fourteen years ago the family decided to sell it forjust EUR25,000, but nobody wanted to buy it either. I met Blandy at a party. and he asked if I'd like to buy the island. Of course I said yes,but I had no money-I was just an art teacher.I tried to find some business partners, who all thought I was crazy.So I sold some of my possessions,put my savings together and bought it.Of course, my family. my friends-all thought I was mad.
When the King originally sold the island,he signed a document, selling all the "possessions and the dominions"of the island.It means I can do what I want with it-I could start a restaurant, or a cinema but nobody thought someone would start a country.So that's what I did:I decided it would be my island, about the size of a one-bedroom house.
I have both a Portuguese passport and one for Pontinha (where my passport number is 0001).There are four citizens: me, my wife, my son and my daughter.I am the police, the gardener,everything.I am whatever I want to be-that's the dream,isn't it?If l want to have a national flag,it could be blue today,red tomorrow.I can change it any time.Of course,my power is only absolute here, where I am the true sovereign.
I don't live in my country full time, but I am often there.My family sometimes drops by, and other people come every day because the country is free for tourists to visit; I never close for bad weather.Sometimes I come here when I'm feeling lively,after a few drinks.
Madeira is surrounded by water,but for some reason we all have to pay to swim in the ocean now,at the swimming spots.However.I have my island,which means I can come swimming whenever I want-it's as if someone has given me the key to the waters.
Our lives are gone in a flash.All change in the world begins with something very small, and this is my country-just a small island.

The new policies aim to mitigate the effects of climate change.
items.explanation: Mitigate는 '완화시키다, 경감하다'라는 뜻으로, 문맥상 '새로운 정책들은 기후 변화의 영향을 완화하는 것을 목표로 한다'가 가장 자연스럽습니다. 악화시키다, 증폭시키다, 야기하다는 문맥에 맞지 않습니다.

items.explanation: 부정어구(Not until the last minute)가 문두로 오면 주어와 동사가 도치됩니다. 과거 시제이므로 'did + 주어 + 동사원형' 형태가 올바릅니다.

items.question:

The decision, ___ by the committee, was met with mixed reactions.
items.explanation: 주어 'the decision'은 위원회에 의해 '만들어지는' 것이므로 수동의 의미를 가지는 과거분사 'made'가 와야 합니다. 이는 관계대명사절 'which was made'가 축약된 형태입니다.

items.explanation: 가정법 과거완료 문장에서 If가 생략되면 주어와 동사가 도치되어 'Had + 주어 + 과거분사' 형태가 됩니다. 주절은 '주어 + would have + 과거분사' 형태로 과거 사실에 대한 반대를 나타냅니다.

items.question: What is the main topic of the passage?
options: The introduction of RFID tracking nametags in Texas schools and the debate surrounding them.
How Texas schools are losing state funding due to inaccurate student attendance records.
The privacy concerns raised by civil liberties groups regarding student tracking technology.
The practical advantages of using advanced technology like nametags in school environments.
items.explanation: 이 지문은 텍사스 학교에서 주 정부 지원금을 확보하기 위해 RFID 추적 명찰을 도입한 것과, 이에 대한 사생활 침해 우려 및 실질적인 이점 등 찬반 논란을 주로 다루고 있습니다.
items.passage:
SAN ANTONIO -- For Tira Starr, an eighth grader at Anson Jones Middle School, the plastic nametag hanging around her neck that she has decorated with a smiley face and a purple bat sticker offers a way to reflect her personal interest. For administrators, it is something else entirely: a device that lets them use radio frequency technology--with scanners tucked behind walls and ceilings--to track her whereabouts. 
Anson Jones is the first school in San Antonio's Northside Independent School District to roll out the new nametags, which are part of a pilot program intended to ensure that the district receives all of the state dollars. 
In Texas, school finance is a numbers game: schools receive money based on the number of students counted in their homeroom classes each morning. At Anson Jones, as at other schools, many students were in school but not in homeroom, so they were not counted and the district lost money, said Pascual Gonzalez, a spokesman for the district. 
"We were leaving money on the table," he said, adding that the district expects a $2 million return on an initial investment of $261,000 in the technology at two pilot schools. 
But the radio frequency identification nametags have prompted concerns from civil liberties groups and electronic privacy watchdogs, which fear a Big Brother atmosphere in Texas public schools. 
Matthew Simpson, a policy strategist for the American Civil Liberties Union of Texas, said the technology was easy to acquire, meaning people outside a school might be able to monitor a student if they obtained the student's unique tracking number. 
Mr. Simpson said the technology was originally designed for shipping goods and for cattle. "It was never intended for people," he said. 
But students and educators at Anson Jones say they are excited about the practical advantages -- getting to eat lunch faster by scanning their bar codes in the lunch line, or being able to locate a child quickly in an emergency. 
Northside is not the first district to use the tracking devices. Two Houston-area districts began the program several years ago. The Spring district, for example, started using the technology in 2004 as a way to track elementary students getting on and off buses. It expanded the program to high school students three years ago and has so far recovered $400,000, said Karen Garrison, a spokeswoman for the district. 
"Our system still focuses on safety but has the added benefit of recovering average daily attendance funding," Ms. Garrison said. 
Wendy Reyes, the principal of Anson Jones, said only one parent had complained about the program at her school. On the first day of classes at Jay High School, home to the other pilot program school in Northside, several parents staged a protest across the street from the school, though most did not have students in the district. 
Many students, teachers and parents at the middle school feel the technology's benefits outweigh privacy concerns, Ms. Reyes said.

items.question: What can be inferred about the primary reason for the author's arrest and subsequent legal charges?
options: The author's refusal to take the breathalyzer test directly led to the arrest and charges.
The author was definitively proven to be driving under the influence of alcohol.
The author failed all of the field sobriety tests administered by the police officer.
The police officer had clear evidence of the author drinking from the bottle in the car.
items.explanation: 지문에서 필자는 음주 측정기 검사를 거부한 것이 '실수'였다고 명시하며, 이후 '경찰관의 명령 불복종'으로 기소되었다고 밝히고 있습니다. 이를 통해 음주 측정 거부가 체포와 법적 기소의 주된 원인이었음을 추론할 수 있습니다.
items.passage:
It was the end of my junior year, the weekend before prom . I was riding with some friends, and a bottle was passed around the car. Everyone was taking swigs . When the bottle got to me, I thought:"What should I do?"I took a swig. It was the biggest mistake of my life. I had to drive home later that night.
I went back to my car, got in and drove off. At a stop sign I saw a policeman sitting in the parking lot across the street. His headlights were turned on, and I knew he was going to follow me. Then he flashed his lights at me. All I could think was: "Oh no, that swig!"
I pulled over and waited for him to come to my door. It felt like forever. "Can I see your license and registration, please, Miss?" I gave them to him. He took them and went back to his car for a while. When he returned, he asked if I had been drinking.
"No," I said. He asked me to step out of my car.
"Walk heel to toe down the white line, please." I passed the test. Next he had me stand on my left foot, lift my right foot and hold it for 30 seconds. I'm not the most coordinated person and I can't even walk and chew gum at the same time, so, needless to say, I didn't pass. Then he asked me to take a breathalyzer test.
That was where I messed up. I told him I didn't want to and didn't understand why I had to. The officer asked me three more times, and I continued to refuse. He told me to turn around and place my hands behind my back. He arrested me right then and there.
The policeman drove me to a police station 20 minutes from my home. He called my parents and told them where I was.
I went to court two months after that, charged with refusing to obey an officer. I got a $700 (4,340 yuan) fine and 40 hours of community service. I'll be on probation for a year, and I'll have to take the driving test again. I lost my license for a whole year.
This was a huge learning experience for me. It opened my eyes to how easy it is to make a stupid decision. I want everyone reading this to know that it's not right to drink and drive. It definitely isn't worth losing your license over.

items.explanation: Diligent는 '성실한, 부지런한'이라는 뜻의 형용사입니다. Lazy는 '게으른', Careless는 '부주의한', Arrogant는 '오만한'이라는 뜻입니다.

items.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 알맞은 단어를 고르시오.
The severe drought had a devastating _____ on the region's agriculture.
items.explanation: 문맥상 '심각한 가뭄이 지역 농업에 파괴적인 ______를 미쳤다'는 의미이므로, '결과'를 뜻하는 consequence가 가장 적절합니다. advantage는 '이점', opportunity는 '기회', foundation은 '기초'라는 뜻입니다.

items.question:
한글 뜻에 맞는 단어를 고르시오.
한글 뜻: 덧없는, 단명하는
items.explanation: Ephemeral은 '덧없는, 단명하는'이라는 뜻으로, 주어진 한글 뜻과 일치합니다. 다른 단어들은 유사한 발음이나 반대 의미를 가진 오답입니다.

items.question:
다음 문장에서 meticulous의 뜻으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
The architect was known for his meticulous attention to detail in every project.
items.explanation: 문맥상 건축가가 '세부 사항에 대한 세심한 주의'로 알려졌다는 내용이 자연스러우므로, meticulous는 '세심한, 꼼꼼한'이라는 의미가 가장 적절합니다. 다른 선택지들은 문맥과 반대되거나 어울리지 않는 의미입니다.

items.question:
다음 문장에서 meticulous의 뜻으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
The artisan was meticulous in his work, ensuring every detail was perfect.
items.explanation: 문맥상 '모든 세부 사항이 완벽하도록 보장했다'는 내용으로 보아, artisan(장인)이 자신의 일에 '세심하고 꼼꼼했다'는 의미가 가장 적절합니다.
